title: Agreeing and Disagreeing
goal: Show agreement, express a different view with the strength you intend, and decide how to continue a disagreement.

rows.text: Signals that the point matches your view.
Acknowledges a useful point; you may still disagree about the conclusion.
Expresses very strong agreement, despite the negative-looking form.

runs.text: Planning a workshop

turns.speaker: Nico

runs.text: We need a room with more seats.

turns.en: We need a room with more seats.

turns.speaker: Harper

runs.text: I agree. Twelve people won't fit comfortably in the small room.

turns.en: I agree. Twelve people won't fit comfortably in the small room.

turns.speaker: Nico

runs.text: And we should check the price first.

turns.en: And we should check the price first.

runs.text: Absolutely.

blocks.caption: Agree with the idea · Nico & Harper

runs.text: You can share a feeling without repeating the whole sentence:
I love this song. — Me too. / So do I.
I don't like crowded rooms. — Me neither. / Neither do I.
I don't think this is a good plan. — I don't think so either.
In the last exchange, both people have doubts about the plan.
I don't think so either
is not a general disagreement answer to every positive statement.
I hear you
and
I know what you mean
can acknowledge someone's experience or concern. Add your view if agreement is unclear:

turns.speaker: Nico

runs.text: I'm worried the bigger room costs too much.

turns.en: I'm worried the bigger room costs too much.

turns.speaker: Harper

runs.text: I hear you. But I still think we need the extra space.

turns.en: I hear you. But I still think we need the extra space.

runs.text: Harper recognizes the concern while maintaining a different conclusion. Listening signals from Chapter 3 do not always equal approval.

rows.text: I agree about the location, but not the price.
Separate the parts you accept and reject.
Say the argument has not persuaded you.

runs.text: A reason can make the difference clear. Direct disagreement is available when you want it; disagreement does not have to start with an apology. Softer wording can still communicate a firm decision.
Discussing a movie

turns.speaker: Nico

runs.text: That was the best part of the movie.

turns.en: That was the best part of the movie.

turns.speaker: Harper

runs.text: I see it differently. I thought the ending was better.

turns.en: I see it differently. I thought the ending was better.

turns.speaker: Nico

runs.text: Really? I thought the ending was too easy.

turns.en: Really? I thought the ending was too easy.

turns.speaker: Harper

runs.text: Fair enough. We liked different things.

turns.en: Fair enough. We liked different things.

runs.text: Fair enough
acknowledges a view or explanation. Here it does not mean Harper changed their taste. Informal
Nah, it wasn't for me
can reject a positive evaluation. Stronger
No way
can make rejection emphatic; surrounding words distinguish that from surprised disbelief.
What makes you think that?
Ask for the reason.
Let's check the information.
Investigate a factual question.
We may have to agree to disagree.
Accept that the views remain different.
Let's leave it there.
End this discussion.
Agreeing to disagree can close a debate about taste. It does not itself establish which factual claim is true or solve a decision the group still needs to make.
Use the supplied roles. Practice both sides alone, then reverse your position.
Someone says
I love quiet cafés
. Your role feels the same. Give a short agreement.
Someone says
I don't like loud music while I'm working
. Your role also dislikes it. Give a negative agreement.
A group needs twelve seats. The small room has eight; the large room has twenty. Someone says
The small room is big enough
. Correct that claim and give the number.

sample.text: No, that's not right. It seats eight, and we have twelve people.

runs.text: A friend says
The movie was boring
. Your role liked the acting but found the ending slow. Give a mixed view. Support:
I liked the acting
the ending was slow
I agree about...

sample.text: I liked the acting, but the ending was slow.

runs.text: They repeat
No, the whole movie was terrible
. Either ask for a reason or close the taste disagreement. Supply the friend's reply:
I didn't care about the characters
or
Okay, let's talk about something else

sample.text: We may have to agree to disagree.

runs.text: Hide Study. Make one exchange showing understanding without agreement, using the expensive-room concern from the model.

sample.text: I hear you, but we still need more seats.

runs.text: Check:
Did your reply agree or disagree with the intended idea? Did you distinguish a person's concern from their conclusion? Could you move the conversation forward without pretending you agreed?
